transcript.text: I have a compliance exception to report. I reviewed the applicable collateral-investment mandate this week and found that the cash collateral may only be placed in government Treasury bills or AAA-rated bank certificates of deposit, each with a maturity of no more than 14 days. The proposed 30-day commercial paper from Delta Financial violates this restriction on two counts -- it's neither Treasury bills nor AAA-rated bank CDs, and its 30-day maturity exceeds the 14-day limit. This restriction has not yet been added to the desk's pre-trade checklist, which is why it wouldn't have been flagged in our standard review process.

transcript.text: I have a client coverage exception to report. I received a client instruction confirmed by email this morning requiring $7,000,000 of this collateral pool to remain as uninvested cash because the client expects a possible securities-loan recall. I have not yet attached the email to the reinvestment ticket. This means the proposed plan to invest the full $25,000,000 would violate the client's instruction -- at most $18,000,000 should be invested, with $7,000,000 held back as cash.

transcript.text: I have an operations exception to report. I confirmed with the settlement team today that the platform can process exactly $12,000,000 of Treasury bills and $6,000,000 of AAA-rated bank certificates of deposit on a T+1 basis, with daily position reconciliation. This capacity confirmation is in an operations note that has not yet been circulated. So if we need to pivot to a compliant reinvestment plan using Treasury bills and AAA bank CDs within the 14-day maturity limit, operations can support up to $18,000,000 total -- $12M in T-bills and $6M in AAA bank CDs -- on a T+1 basis with daily reconciliation.
